chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Lena Horne asks him to be her pianist and arranger
summary: Staying at Juan Tizol's house, Horace met Lena Horne again through Rose Tizol; she offered him a tour of RKO theatres and Chez Paris and paid far more than he'd have asked.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: -- Duke Ellington. I was stopping at his home, and I knew his wife Rose Tizol. She was quite a comedian, you know, natural comedian. I don't mean like a professional comedian. She was funny, and she and Lena Horne were very good friends, and Lena often came over and this is how I ran into Lena. I hadn't seen her since the days of Charley Barnet. And she came over one day to see Rose Tizol, and incidentally, she had a two room apartment over the garage in the back that she was renting to a movie star. Guess who? You remember a guy named Willie Best that played the funny parts with the big goo-goo eyes and the comical things?
Well, Willie Best had that apartment, and we used to talk. Well anyway, Lena came over to visit Juan Tizol's wife, Rose, one day, and I was in the house

talking, like we're talking, you know, and she wanted to know what I was doing there. I told her (unintelligible) I got here with Fletcher, and I was getting ready to leave, and she says, "What are you gonna go back?" she says, "I'm getting ready to make a tour," she says. "Why don't you join me?" And I was a little quiet, you know, because it took my breath. She thought I was thinkin' about it. This is funny. So she said, "Come on, let's go in the room and talk." So she took me in the room, and we talked, and she said, "Listen, I'm gonna make a tour of theatres, RKO, all of the United States, and then I'm going into Chicago to the Chez Paris," and she says, "I'd like for you to be my pianist and arranger, and I'll pay you for each arrangement you make, make as many as you want to, wanna, and one of those things. I'll pay you for the recordings, and all these things, and I was so dumb-founded, I couldn't talk. She thought I was --
-- debating over the thing, you know.
So she says, "I'll double your salary."

So she asked me, was. How much money I wanted, you know. I didn't say anything. So I'm glad I didn't, because what she came out with, and I don't want the Internal Revenue to be listening, but what she came out with -- it was far more than I would have asked. And man, I didn't say anything, that got me then. She says, "Well, I'm gonna give you extra for
so and so when I get it." (Inaudible) So, man, I still can't talk; I'm silent. (LAUGHTER)
